h1:
Uthai Thani Cafes
8 Riverside & Old Town Spots
intro: Uthai Thani is one of those small towns where time genuinely slows down once you sit with a coffee. The charm is the Sakae Krang River, lined on both banks with old teak houseboats, plus an old town that still has wooden shophouses and little lanes to wander. We've picked 8 cafes that are actually open right now — both floating spots with houseboat views and coffee shops tucked into Trok Rong Ya — with their standout menus and the prices we actually saw.

blocks.html: People like to call Uthai Thani a slow-life town, and that's not an exaggeration — the heart of it is the Sakae Krang River, where a houseboat community has genuinely lived for over a hundred years. So the best cafes here aren't just selling coffee; they're selling the view of wooden houseboats floating on the water and the breeze off the river. Over in the old town around Trok Rong Ya and the walking street, there are small cafes where owners have renovated old wooden buildings themselves — the kind of place that feels like dropping by a friend's house. We've split everything into two clear zones, riverside and old town, so you can pick whichever mood fits the day.

Ordered from the clearest river-and-houseboat views and most talked-about spots, down to old town cafes that stand out for atmosphere and coffee. The prices listed are what we actually saw, and they can shift a little depending on the menu and the time of day.

items.name: Mum Sakae
items.blurb: The Sakae Krang riverside cafe most people think of first. It's a two-storey octagonal wooden pavilion — the ground floor is open-air, while upstairs has an air-conditioned zone and a balcony with bar stools where you can dangle your legs and take in 360-degree views of the bridge over the river and the houseboats. The standout is Malay-style roti with a thick, soft texture, the coffee is good, and there are halal savoury dishes like chicken biryani (weekends only).
items.meta: By Wat Ubosatharam bridge · Open daily 07.00–18.00

items.name: Baan Phae Sakae Krang Cafe & Homestay
items.blurb: A floating cafe converted from a genuine teak houseboat that's nearly a hundred years old. You can sip your coffee on the raft and dip your feet in the water, with locals' houseboats floating in rows all around you — it's the most authentic riverside-community feel of any spot here. There's fresh coffee, fruit smoothies and freshly baked goods, and if you want to stay over, there's a homestay right on the raft.
items.meta: On the Sakae Krang River · Open daily 07.00–17.30

items.name: Tone Café
items.blurb: A cafe in a small lane off the Trok Rong Ya walking street, decorated vintage-style with old wooden doors and windows salvaged from former houses. The vibe is as warm as visiting a friend who takes coffee seriously — they use Chiang Rai arabica beans, and the signature worth trying is coffee mixed with tamarind juice or honey bitter orange, sour-sweet and refreshing.
items.meta: Soi Suk Kasem, Trok Rong Ya · 08.30–16.30 (closed Tue)

items.name: X-bar Cafe'
items.blurb: A modern black-and-brown toned cafe in the old town that opens early at seven, perfect for early risers who want coffee before walking the market. The highlight is coffee shots mixed with various fruit juices — bright and sour, cutting through any richness.
items.meta: Soi Rak Kading, Uthai Mai · Open daily 07.00–16.30

items.name: Boo Bun
items.blurb: A bright American red-and-blue toned shop whose standout is handmade bread and pastries, baked fresh in-house. A good stop for a croissant or bread with morning coffee before you carry on walking Trok Rong Ya.
items.meta: Soi Suk Kasem, Uthai Mai · 08.30–16.30 (closed Tue)

items.name: Thai-Thai Dessert Café
items.blurb: A homey, mostly wood-decorated cafe in Trok Rong Ya, across from Je Nok's chicken noodles. There are plenty of cute photo corners, and beyond coffee, tea and Italian soda, they also serve rice dishes and Thai desserts to order alongside — a good spot to rest after walking the market.
items.meta: Trok Rong Ya, Uthai Mai · Open late morning–evening

items.name: FFF's Cafe
items.blurb: A serious matcha cafe in town. If you like your green deep and slightly bitter, the matcha latte and green tea menu here come out genuinely strong — a solid option for people who don't drink coffee. The shop is small and compact, but comfortable to sit in.

items.name: Dayla Roti
items.blurb: Not a fancy cafe, but a Pakistani roti shop over 90 years old that's worth a stop. The roti — crisp outside, soft inside — goes with hot tea or coffee, and it's an old town bite that gives you more flavour and story than looks. If you love the truly traditional places, this one will win you over.

items.name: Thasung Coffee
items.blurb: A small coffee shop belonging to Wat Thasung, tucked into the riverside zone by the temple's old ordination hall, across the road from the main complex. What reviewers talk about most isn't just the coffee but the crew — teachers and students take turns behind the bar, and profits go into the school's scholarship fund. Iced americanos start at 45 baht, and there's a quiet air-conditioned room with Wi-Fi, an easy leg-rest after walking the temple grounds.
items.meta: Wat Thasung riverside zone, Sakae Krang River · Open 08:00–16:00 (till 17:00 Sat–Sun)

items.name: River Lake Café & Restaurant
items.blurb: The café at Uthai River Lake Resort on Ko Thepho, the big island wrapped by the Chao Phraya and Sakae Krang rivers. Tables face the resort's lake, with a wooden pier, swings and hammocks for a slow photo stroll along the water. You don't need to be a hotel guest — walk-ins are welcome, and the menu runs from fresh coffee and desserts to proper mains (the big kitchen starts around 11am). A handy pit stop on the Ko Thepho cycling loop.

blocks.text: Sakae Krang Riverside — Watching the Houseboats

blocks.html: If you're coming to Uthai Thani mainly for the riverside view, pin the first two: Mum Sakae and Baan Phae Sakae Krang. Both sit right on the Sakae Krang River — not just looking at water in the distance. Mum Sakae stands out for its two-storey octagonal pavilion with 360-degree views and savoury food to fill up on, while Baan Phae Sakae Krang stands out as a genuine wooden raft on the water where you can dip your feet — and it's closer to the houseboat community.

blocks.title: When the view looks best
blocks.html: Go early, before nine — the sun is still soft, the water is still, the houseboats reflect beautifully, and it isn't hot yet. The other good window is late afternoon, around four to five, when golden light hits the houseboats: great for photos and a cool, comfortable breeze. Midday the sun is harsh and hot, so if you go then, choose a covered or air-conditioned zone.

The nice thing about the riverside cafes here is that they're not expensive — most drinks run from the low tens up to ฿70, but you get a view you won't find in a big city. One thing to know: these are wooden rafts by the water, so the floor may have gaps and shift a little. If you bring small kids or older folks, watch the edge of the raft and hold the railings.

blocks.text: Old Town & Trok Rong Ya — Walking and Sipping

blocks.html: Trok Rong Ya is a small walking-street lane in Uthai Thani's old town, lined on both sides with old wooden buildings and shophouses, many of which have turned into cafes and dessert shops. Walking the whole lane takes under ten minutes, but there are several cafes to stop at along the way. The charm is that most are owner-run, renovated from the original buildings while keeping the wooden frames and old doors and windows — so each has its own warm, distinct feel.

items.name: Tone Café
items.blurb: Vintage old wood, Chiang Rai arabica coffee, and a standout of coffee mixed with tamarind and honey bitter orange.

items.name: Boo Bun
items.blurb: Freshly baked handmade bakery in a bright, cheerful shop — good for a morning stop before walking the market.

items.name: Thai-Thai Dessert Café
items.blurb: Homey and woody, with Thai desserts and rice dishes and plenty of photo corners.

items: Walk Trok Rong Ya on Saturday evening — it becomes a walking street with extra food and souvenirs, several cafes are still open, and the atmosphere is livelier than on weekdays.
Old town cafes close early — many shut around 4.30–5pm, so if you want to linger, go in the afternoon and don't leave it too late.
Check the weekly closing day — small shops like Tone Café and Boo Bun are closed on Tuesdays, so plan around it.

blocks.html: Want to catch both the riverside views and the old town in one go? This works nicely — start by the river in the morning when the light is soft, then walk into the old town later in the morning.

items.activity: Start at Baan Phae Sakae Krang or Mum Sakae, sip coffee by the river in the soft morning light and photograph the houseboats.
items.note: Still water, few people, the best view of the day.

items.activity: Cross to the town side and wander Wat Ubosatharam right by the bridge, taking in the murals and the riverside temple atmosphere.
Head into Trok Rong Ya, stop at Boo Bun or X-bar for bread and a second coffee, and look at the old wooden buildings.
items.note: The bakeries bake fresh in the morning.

items.activity: Finish at Tone Café, relax in the vintage room and try the tamarind or honey bitter-orange coffee.
items.note: Before the midday sun gets harsh.

blocks.title: Getting there / parking
blocks.html: The old town and the riverside cafes are very close together — you can walk between almost all of them. Driving yourself is easiest; you can park near the municipal market or along the streets in town. If you don't have a car, renting a bicycle or motorbike in town is plenty, since the distances are short and the town isn't crowded.

faq.q: Which Uthai Thani cafe has the best houseboat view?
faq.a: For a clear houseboat view, we recommend Mum Sakae, a two-storey octagonal pavilion with 360-degree views, and Baan Phae Sakae Krang, a floating cafe on a genuine wooden raft where you can dip your feet in the water. Both sit right on the Sakae Krang River — not just looking at water in the distance.

faq.q: Are the Sakae Krang riverside cafes expensive?
faq.a: No. Most drinks run around ฿40–75, and you'll rarely spend more than ฿100 per person — cheap by the numbers, but with a river-and-houseboat view you won't find in a big city.

faq.q: What hours do the Trok Rong Ya cafes keep, and which days are they closed?
faq.a: Most open late-morning around 08.30 and close around 16.30. Some, like Tone Café and Boo Bun, are closed on Tuesdays, while X-bar opens early at 07.00 every day. We'd check the weekly closing day before going, and visit in the afternoon since many shops close in the early evening.

faq.q: Can I do the Uthai Thani cafe scene without a car?
faq.a: Easily — the riverside cafes and the old town are very close together, and you can walk between almost all of them. Otherwise, renting a bicycle or motorbike in town is plenty. The town isn't crowded and the distances are short.

faq.q: Can I bring small kids or older relatives to a floating cafe?
faq.a: You can, but these are wooden rafts by the water, so the floor may have gaps and shift a little — watch the edge of the raft and hold the railings. If you'd rather sit somewhere more stable, Mum Sakae, a pavilion on the bank, is the safer bet.
